To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) nc-Si:H can be deposited on PEN substrates without intentional heating, but the microstructure and electrical properties are different from that of samples grown on glass, and (ii) the deposition of doped layers on PEN substrates at room temperature is possible but only with very thick layers.

we found that intrinsic layers of nc-Si:H can be deposited at room temperature on PEN and glass substrates, and that the electrical conductivity of doped layers is strongly dependent on the deposition temperature.
we were able to deposit intrinsic and doped nc-Si:H on glass and PEN, and that we found that substrate temperature has to be higher than 100 °C to achieve good electrical properties for thin layers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the properties of thin films grown on plastic substrates, and the development of devices based on these films.
the development of low temperature deposition processes and the study of the electrical and structural properties of a-Si:H, nc-Si:H and doped layers.
a new approach to the growth of intrinsic, p-type and n-type doped layers, and with the electrical and structural characterization of these materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the growth of a-Si:H/nc-Si:H on PEN is feasible and that it can be done without intentional heating, but with a higher degree of disorder than in glass substrates.
the deposition conditions for intrinsic a-Si:H layers on PEN and on substrates without intentional heating are not the same.

the transition between a- and nc-Si is not abrupt but gradual and that the transition temperature depends on the substrate and on the deposition conditions, and that the electrical properties of the films are also affected by the substrate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the deposition conditions and substrate material play an important role on the structural and electrical quality of the material.
the deposition of a-Si:H on glass and PEN substrates at room temperature and without intentional heating is a feasible approach, but the electrical properties are still not good.

, for the growth of intrinsic layers close to the transition region between a-Si and nc-Si, it is necessary to deposit the layers on substrates at temperatures higher than 200 °C, while for doped layers, it is not possible to obtain high doping levels without heating the substrates.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the transition from a-Si:H to nc-Si:H occurs for a-Si:H deposited on PEN substrates at lower temperature than that observed in a-Si:H films deposited on glass, and that this transition can be used for the deposition of doped films on PEN at lower temperature.
the deposition of intrinsic, p- and n-doping layers of nc-Si:H at low temperature is possible and can lead to devices with improved performance.
, with the proper deposition parameters, nc-Si:H can be deposited on PEN at room temperature, with good structural and electrical properties.
